questions.text: The rotation of the earth on its axis is responsible for
options: the varying length of the year
questions.explanation: One rotation every twenty-four hours brings each meridian into and out of sunlight.

questions.text: Lines of longitude are used mainly to determine
questions.explanation: The earth turns 15° each hour, so every 15° of longitude represents one hour of time difference.

questions.explanation: Granite and basalt are igneous rocks formed from molten material.

questions.explanation: The Niger Delta is a classic example, formed where the river loses velocity on entering the sea.

questions.text: The instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure is the
questions.explanation: A barometer measures pressure; falling pressure often signals approaching bad weather.

questions.text: The harmattan wind that affects West Africa between November and February blows from the
questions.explanation: It is a dry, dusty north-easterly wind originating over the Sahara.

questions.text: The vegetation belt found in the extreme north of Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Rainfall declines northwards, giving Sudan savanna and, at the far north-east, Sahel scrub.

questions.text: The difference between birth rate and death rate gives the
questions.explanation: Natural increase excludes migration, which is counted separately in population change.

questions.text: Population density is correctly expressed as
options: total population divided by land area
land area divided by total population
urban population divided by rural population
questions.explanation: Density is usually stated as persons per square kilometre.

questions.text: A settlement pattern in which houses are strung out along a road or river is described as
questions.explanation: Linear settlements follow a line of communication or a water source.

questions.text: Nigeria's tin mining is associated mainly with
questions.explanation: Alluvial tin and columbite have long been worked on the Jos Plateau.

questions.text: The chief advantage of inland water transport is that it is
options: available in every part of a country
questions.explanation: Water transport is slow but carries heavy, bulky cargo at low cost per tonne-kilometre.

questions.text: Desertification in northern Nigeria is worsened mainly by
questions.explanation: Removal of vegetation cover exposes fragile soils to wind erosion and southward desert encroachment.

questions.explanation: The Equator is latitude 0° and divides the globe north from south.

questions.text: The revolution of the earth around the sun gives rise to
questions.explanation: The earth's tilted axis combined with its annual orbit varies the concentration of sunlight received.

questions.text: Rainfall formed when moist air is forced to rise over a mountain barrier is
questions.explanation: Relief or orographic rainfall falls on the windward slope, leaving a rain shadow to leeward.

questions.text: Limestone, which is quarried for cement production, is an example of
questions.explanation: It forms from accumulated shells and organic remains compacted over time.

questions.text: A steep-sided valley with an almost vertical wall cut by a river in a dry region is a
questions.explanation: Rapid vertical erosion with little lateral erosion produces a gorge or canyon.

questions.text: Shifting cultivation is practised mainly because
options: it allows exhausted land to regain fertility
questions.explanation: Land is cropped for a few seasons, then abandoned to bush fallow while the farmer moves on.

questions.text: An industry that is located close to its source of raw material is said to be
questions.explanation: Bulky or perishable raw materials, as in cement and sugar milling, pull the factory to the source.

questions.text: A major problem of road transport in Nigeria is
options: poor maintenance of the road network
the small size of the country
questions.explanation: Potholes, flooding and weak maintenance raise costs, travel time and accident rates.

questions.text: The Kainji Dam on the River Niger was built principally to
questions.explanation: Hydro-electricity is its chief purpose, with navigation, fishing and irrigation as additional benefits.

questions.text: The bearing of a point due east of an observer is
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north, so east is 090°.

questions.text: Gully erosion is most severe in which part of Nigeria?
options: The South East, especially around Anambra and Enugu
questions.explanation: Friable sandy soils on steep slopes with heavy rainfall have produced extensive gullies in the South East.

questions.text: Rural–urban migration in Nigeria is caused mainly by
options: better employment prospects in the cities
lower population density in the cities
questions.explanation: Job opportunities, schools and services pull young people to towns, while low rural incomes push them out.
